values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pickerellakekalkaska ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Pickerel Lake State Forest Campground, Kalkaska: rustic, open all year, managed by Hartwick Pines SP 989-348-7068, 13 sites, $20, ORV operation between SFCG and trails 'yes', boat ramp 'R', 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pickerellakekalkaska ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pickerellakekalkaska ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + amenity table (Pickerel Lake, Kalkaska: 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 13 sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pickerellakekalkaska ('There are 13 sites for tent and small trailer use.' 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site.') + amenity table (13 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic campground on the shore of Pickerel Lake, shaded by hardwoods and birch, 13.5 mi N of Kalkaska via CR-612 and Sunset Trail Rd. Concrete boat launch on the NW side. Campers report 22-ft rigs fit some sites. The Kalkaska Trail Route (ORV) can be reached near the campground. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: $20 (confirmed), no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 13 sites (all confirmed, derived -> manual); 15-day max (inherited, now stated). Sites are 'for tent and small trailer use' (boilerplate, silent on length). Season 'open all year' (roads not plowed) already manual, left. Not equestrian. ORV operation between the campground and trails is allowed (amenity table 'yes'; Kalkaska Trail Route nearby), but the DNR doesn't describe it as an ORV trail camp. Access via CR-612 and Sunset Trail Rd, no road warning. Note trimmed of field restatements.
flags: Phone: the entry has none. The DNR campground page and the amenity table give 989-348-7068 (Hartwick Pines State Park, the managing park).
